teaser.text: A bank sells access to money: it keeps deposits, makes loans, moves payments, and manages investments. China Merchants Bank Co. Ltd. earns when those services produce interest and fees, but bears the risks of funding, defaults, and withdrawals.

stock.meta_description: CMB's weighted forecast points to HK$54.60 in October 2027, with bear, base and bull cases shaped by margins, credit costs and confidence.
stock.opening: The weighted scenario points to HK$54.60 in October 2027, a 5% total return including dividends. It hinges on margins, credit costs and investor confidence.
stock.closing: The full memo explains CMB’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could CMB's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is HK$54.60 in October 2027, HK$56.86 in October 2028, and HK$59.52 in October 2029. Including dividends, those outcomes represent returns of 5%, 14%, and 23% from today’s HK$53.80. The final scenario weights are 30% for the bear case, 52% for the base case, and 18% for the bull case.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for CMB?

paragraphs.text: The base case uses 4.5% annual earnings growth and retains 65% of earnings, consistent with the supplied analyst outlook and the recent 35% payout policy. Book value reaches RMB1,274,800 million in October 2027 and RMB1,376,400 million in October 2028. It reaches RMB1,482,500 million in October 2029. The bear case ends at RMB1,403,000 million because margin pressure and credit losses reduce retained earnings. The bull case reaches RMB1,533,300 million because margin stabilization, recurring wealth fees and contained losses lift earnings.

The bull case requires deposit repricing and firmer loan demand to stabilize NIM. Wealth fees must remain recurring, digital efficiency must become real cost savings, and credit losses must stay contained. The share price reaches HK$64.57 in October 2027 and HK$88.40 by October 2029. Its 18% probability reflects the need for several conditions to succeed together while credit charges remain elevated and retail profit is under pressure.

blocks.heading: How much cash does CMB really make?

paragraphs.subsection: 5.9 — Cash flow and earnings available to ordinary shareholders
paragraphs.text: A deposit brings cash into the bank but also creates an obligation to repay the customer. A loan sends cash out but creates a financial asset. That is why CMB’s 2025 operating cash flow reached RMB451,457 million, well above profit after tax of RMB151,126 million. The cash surplus mainly reflects funding movements, not money freely available for dividends.

paragraphs.subsection: 5.9 — Cash flow and earnings available to ordinary shareholders
paragraphs.text: Common shareholders’ equity reached RMB1,095,418 million in 2025, while net asset value per share was RMB43.43. CMB is therefore accumulating equity while earning a lower return on it. The specialist’s final reading is balanced: the bank has scale, funding and buffers, but its future depends on restoring asset yields without allowing credit pressure to consume those strengths.

blocks.heading: How much does CMB pay per share over time?

paragraphs.text: Assets grew about 9.0% a year from 2021 to 2025, while revenue grew about 0.3% a year. NIM fell from 2.5% in 2021 to 1.9% in 2025, though lower credit charges supported profit. Diluted EPS rose from RMB4.61 in 2021 to RMB5.70 in 2025. The 2025 dividend was RMB2.02 per share. Market value applies the H-share price to all ordinary shares although A shares are 81.80% of the company.

paragraphs.text: Management therefore links asset growth, asset returns, capital and payouts. The 2026 interim dividend is set at 35% of first-half profit attributable to ordinary shareholders. That rule offers meaningful income while leaving part of the earnings inside the bank.

blocks.heading: What is CMB's dividend yield against its price?

paragraphs.text: China Merchants Bank is a Chinese bank whose share price asks investors to trust both its profits and its balance sheet. At HK$53.80, the question is not simply whether the stock looks cheap, but what must remain true for that price to work.

The calculated market value is based on the H-share price applied to every ordinary share, although A shares make up 81.80% of the company and H shares 18.20%. Cash flow and net debt also mislead here: deposits fund loans but remain money owed to customers. Capital, loan losses and distributable profit matter more; the dividend yield is 4.4%.

earnings.title: CMB earnings: guidance and what to watch
earnings.meta_description: CMB’s October 31, 2026 results will test deposit and loan growth, margins and credit costs.
earnings.opening: CMB’s next results are expected on October 31, 2026. Watch whether loan growth earns enough to offset margin pressure and credit costs.
earnings.closing: The full memo also explains CMB’s business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: On 27 March 2026, CMB targeted growth of approximately 6% to 7% in total customer deposits and total loans and advances during 2026. Deposits are money customers place with the bank; loans are money the bank lends. Growing both can enlarge the business, but it creates value only when the income from loans covers deposit costs, operating expenses, expected losses and the capital tied up in lending.

blocks.heading: Has CMB kept its dividend promises?

paragraphs.text: CMB’s stated dividend policy generally sets a minimum cash distribution of 30% of attributable profit. The bank said its payout remained above 35% since 2024 and that it introduced an interim dividend in 2025. That supports shareholder cash returns, but the unchanged 0.94% non-performing-loan ratio did not prevent problem-loan balances from increasing.

blocks.heading: What do CMB’s last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: The first half tells the same story. Revenue rose 3.9%, while profit rose 2.0%. Credit charges increased 18.5%. NIM was 1.8% in both 2026 quarters, compared with 1.9% in the corresponding 2025 quarters. More earning assets and cheaper funding supported income, but pricing had not clearly recovered.

blocks.heading: What should CMB watchers look for next?

paragraphs.text: The next earnings announcement is expected on 27 October 2026. Investors should look together at loan balances, lending margins, impairment charges and capital. A larger loan book with weaker returns would tell a very different story from growth that replenishes capital.
